transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-09
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jared Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Evan Stone (Redwood Product), Lena Ortiz (CTO, NimbleWare), Marcus Hale (Staff ML Eng, NimbleWare), Sofia Kim (PM, NimbleWare)

Summary:
Quick hands-on demo of Redwood Console focused on typed response contracts (JSON mode), tool invocation patterns, and runtime guardrails. Customer is evaluating hosted vs private deployment for a search/assist product; main concerns: latency under 200ms p50 for short queries, data residency, and predictable cost. Agreed to pilot: console sandbox + schema template + pilot pricing.

Topics covered:
- Typed contracts / JSON mode: why enforced schemas reduce downstream validation work
- Tool/function calling flows: safe tool invocation and fallbacks
- Guardrails & runtime: rollouts, circuit-breakers, fallback models
- Console walkthrough: schema editor, contract testing, simulated invokes
- Optimize suggestions: batching, kv/prefix cache, quantization tradeoffs
- Security/compliance: SAML SSO, SOC 2, KMS integration, audit logs

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Jared from Redwood, i'll kick off real quick then priya will do a live run in the console.
[00:00:08] Lena: thanks, Jared. We have about an hour, want to see the typed outputs piece — we've been struggling with schema drift in prod.
[00:00:15] Marcus: and curious about performance implications, right now our p50 is about 180ms for short prompts on our infra but cost is high.
[00:00:20] Priya: great, that's exactly what we'll show — typed contracts reduce parsing errors and eliminate a class of downstream bugs, and the console has tools to test contract regressions before you push.
[00:00:30] Evan: i'll share a quick diagram in chat — link: https://redwood.com/s/typed-demo (internal demo deck)
[00:00:36] Speaker 2: (background) yep received.
[00:00:42] Priya: ok i'm switching to the Console — first thing you'll see is the schema editor. we can author a json schema for the assistant response, specify types, enums, nested objects, all that. i'll paste a simple invoice extraction schema to show.
[00:01:05] Priya: one nice bit is the playground run with 'strict' mode — if the model emits extra fields or wrong types, console flags it and you can record that as a regression.
[00:01:20] Marcus: is strict enforced at runtime or only in the sandbox?
[00:01:22] Priya: you can choose. strict in sandbox is for tests; for runtime you can set the route to "reject" or "coerce" or "fallback". so if outputs don't validate, you can route to a fallback model, call a repair tool, or return an error to client.
[00:01:38] Lena: fallback to a smaller model is interesting for cost. what about latency when falling back?
[00:01:42] Priya: good question — we support parallel invoke: primary model + cheap verifier in parallel, whichever returns valid first wins. that keeps p50 low while protecting correctness, but it does increase unit cost a bit.
[00:01:58] Sofia: can we call our internal enrichment service from the model? we have a product catalog API with product ids that need to be resolved.
[00:02:05] Priya: yes that's where tool/function calling comes in — we demoed the tool sandbox earlier; you register an HTTP tool with an input/response contract, the model returns a tool invocation JSON, Redwood validates it, executes the tool in an isolated runtime, validates tool output against a response schema, and then resumes the model with the tool result.
[00:02:26] Marcus: any safety around arbitrary outbound calls? we can't have model call arbitrary domains.
[00:02:30] Priya: absolutely — tool registry is whitelist-only per workspace, can be network-scoped to VPC endpoints, and execution runs in a sandboxed environment; plus audit logs show every invocation.
[00:02:41] Lena: and KMS for keys?
[00:02:43] Jared: yes we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for secrets; SSO via SAML; full audit logs with retention policy as an add-on.
[00:02:52] [00:03:00] Priya: i'm switching to a live example now — nimble search assistant: prompt + json contract for answer blocks (id, title, snippet, score). running a test set now so you can see validation failures.
[00:03:18] Priya: notice this run flagged a missing 'id' on two responses; i can open the correction flow which will attempt a repair prompt, or mark as a regression to block rollout.
[00:03:30] Marcus: what's the repair latency impact?
[00:03:33] Priya: repair is usually a small extra call — if you run repair synchronously it adds ~50-120ms depending on model; we also support async repair pipelines where the client gets a best-effort result and a followup corrected payload.
[00:03:48] Evan: i'm dropping the pilot template now — includes sample schemas, rollout policy, and an Optimize report for batching suggestions. link: https://redwood.com/s/pilot-template-nimbleware
[00:03:58] Sofia: nice. about Optimize — will it analyze our traffic traces and recommend batch sizes?
[00:04:03] Priya: yes, Optimize ingests token distribution and sequence length histograms, suggests batching and kv cache configs, and simulates cost/latency tradeoffs. we'll run it against your traces in the sandbox.
[00:04:15] Marcus: we have bursty traffic — evenings spike 4x, can we keep p95 under 400ms?
[00:04:21] Jared: with Dedicated capacity + autoscale you can provision a baseline and burst pool. there's also graceful degradation — route to cheaper model variants during overload, or serve cached answers from prefix cache.
[00:04:34] Lena: about private deployment — we have EU data residency requirements, plus an internal security review. how invasive is the private control plane?
[00:04:42] Jared: Private offers a customer-managed control plane in your VPC, optional on-prem worker nodes; we do a transfer of the minimal agent. network policies can ensure data never transits public infra. we'll share our architecture diagram and an install checklist.
[00:04:57] Lena: good, SOC2 is a must, and we need to see auditability for tool invocations.
[00:05:02] Priya: audit logs include every model call, schema validation result, tool invocation and response; logs are queryable in the Console and can stream to your SIEM.
[00:05:12] [00:05:30] Speaker 1: (lena) ok can you show how to author a contract that includes a typed 'actions' array for follow-up calls? we do structured actions a lot.
[00:05:36] Priya: sure — here's an actions array schema with fields: name:string, params:object (validated), provenance token. Console enforces param schemas per action so downstream systems get typed data.
[00:05:50] Marcus: will the model ever hallucinate tool names, like inventing a tool that doesn't exist?
[00:05:55] Priya: we prevent that by limiting tool names to the registry; model returns a tool_id and params, and if it's not in registry the invoke is rejected. we also expose a 'most-likely' suggestion mode in the editor for training but it's not allowed in production routes.
[00:06:10] Sofia: what's the debugging workflow? my team will need to iterate quickly on schemas.
[00:06:13] Priya: Console has a 'contract test' harness where you can run batches of prompts, see validation diffs, and export failing examples. there's also an incremental test runner that can be added to your CI.
[00:06:25] Jared: quick commercial note — pilot pricing is typically a small committed bucket of Dedicated time or a hosted pilot with usage caps. i'll follow up with a tailored price that reflects your expected p50/p95 and traffic patterns.
[00:06:38] Lena: sounds good. any competitor differences to highlight?
[00:06:41] Jared: some competitors do schema validation client-side or in post-processing; Redwood enforces it as a first-class runtime primitive and couples it with tool registry + guardrails. also stronger observability for token-level cost attribution.
[00:06:55] Marcus: can we run an A/B where half calls go to our current infra and half to Redwood hosted to compare latency/cost?
[00:07:00] Priya: yes, we can set up a canary/traffic split in the rollout policy. you'll get per-route metrics.
[00:07:06] [00:07:20] Priya: ok i'm going to demonstrate a tool call now — model emits an invoke for product-resolve tool, console validates, executes, returns structured product object, resume prompt returns final JSON.
[00:07:34] Marcus: i see the trace — neat, and the tool output was validated against the product schema, which prevents downstream parsing errors.
[00:07:40] Priya: exactly. i'm toggling the 'reject on invalid' policy to show a blocked rollout scenario — this would prevent a new model from being promoted until tests pass.
[00:07:52] Sofia: we'll definitely want that for the customer-facing assistant.
[00:07:56] Lena: what about latency SLOs and alerts?
[00:07:59] Evan: Console exposes per-route SLOs and alert conditions; you can attach runbook links and escalation policies.
[00:08:08] Marcus: any gotchas for long-tail sequences? our tickets sometimes have 2k token histories.
[00:08:12] Priya: long sequences change batching and kv cache behavior. Optimize will flag those routes and recommend quantized model variants or KV sharding; for very long context, we recommend a retrieval-augmented flow with a short context window.
[00:08:26] [00:08:40] Lena: ok, let's talk timeline — we want a pilot inside 2 weeks if feasible.
[00:08:44] Jared: we can do sandbox in 3 business days once we have the sample prompts and SAML details; pilot pricing and SOC2 package i'll send by Friday (2025-09-12).
[00:08:57] Marcus: will we need to sign an NDA for sample data?
[00:09:00] Jared: we can accept anonymized traces first; NDA is optional but we do have customer confidentiality agreements.
[00:09:06] [00:09:20] Sofia: any docs I should review?
[00:09:23] Priya: i'll drop these links in chat: Pilot template, Console contract guide, Optimize report example.
[00:09:30] Evan: links: https://redwood.com/s/pilot-template-nimbleware, https://redwood.com/s/console-contracts, https://redwood.com/s/optimize-sample
[00:09:36] Lena: thanks.
[00:09:40] [00:09:50] Jared: ok quick recap and next steps — 1) Jared send pricing + SOC2/KMS/SAML docs by 2025-09-12; 2) Priya provision console sandbox + schema template by 2025-09-15; 3) Marcus share sample prompt set and token histograms by 2025-09-16; 4) follow-up checkpoint scheduled next Wed 2025-09-17 16:00 UTC.
[00:10:15] Marcus: perfect.
[00:10:18] Lena: looking forward to it.
[00:10:20] Jared: thanks all. we'll wrap but we'll stay in chat for any immediate follow-ups.

End of transcript (partial automated notes + live typing).
